prompt: Act as an Ancient Greek philologist writing learner-facing contextual glosses. The input is one ten-column CoNLL-U block: ID, FORM, LEMMA, coarse POS, XPOS, FEATS, HEAD, DEPREL, DEPS, MISC. Return exactly one tab-separated line for each real source-token row, in input order: ID, a tab, then one concise English gloss. A real source token has a MISC value beginning t_. An artificial omitted-structure row has a MISC value beginning e_: omit that row completely, even when its FORM looks like [0], [1], or [2]. IDs in the response may therefore skip numbers. Express the contextual sense and materially relevant morphology or syntax, not merely the lemma: examples of the desired style include of-Peleus'-son, to-Marcus, for-them, to-each-other, was-writing, and one-must. Supply an elided argument only when context requires it and mark it in brackets. Do not absorb meaning belonging to a separate overt token. Use hyphens instead of spaces inside one gloss. Keep proper names capitalized. Gloss punctuation with the punctuation character. Never copy a non-punctuation Greek FORM as its gloss. Copy each included row's ID from column one; never number response lines by their position. For this five-block calibration set the required IDs are fixed: sentence_id 1 uses 1–8 and 10; sentence_id 2 uses 1–13 and 15; sentence_id 3 uses 1–21 and 23; sentence_id 4 uses 1–12 and 14; sentence_id 5 uses 1–26 and 28. The final punctuation must therefore keep ID 10, 15, 23, 14, or 28 respectively, never the preceding artificial ID. Return no artificial rows, CoNLL-U rows, JSON, Markdown, blank lines, or explanation, and never put a tab or newline inside a gloss.
